newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha hits five-year high on crude surge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha hits five-year high on crude surge.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices hit their highest level in five years, lifted by a crude surge on overnight overseas crude markets as well as brisk physical demand for December delivery cargoes, traders said on Thursday.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half January delivery was assessed at $230.00/232.00, surpassing the previous high of $223.50/225.00.
Second-half January was indicated at about $2.00 lower than the first-half January level.
In spreads, first-half January/first-half February was discussed at plus $3.00/5.00.
In physical naphtha trading, a Japanese oil firm said it bought a spot cargo to be delivered to Kawasaki, near Tokyo, in second-half December. The price was not available.

In middle distillates, a major refiner was believed to have bought two jet kerosene cargoes for December arrival at around $1.50 above the mean of Singapore quotes. One of them will be delivered to Japan's northernmost island of Hokkaido, where kerosene demand picks up earlier than the rest of the country for heating purposes, traders said. The other cargo will be shipped to the Tokyo area, they added.
